text:
maria: Hey team — replays using our prod trace on the new kernel-selection patch show a weird latency bump when we run through the proxy. P95 jumps ~4x. Suspect client-side connection churn + Nagle + TLS handshake pileup. Anyone seen this when comparing grpc replay vs synthetic http keepalive runs? :thinking:
kevin: can you paste the load harness cmd + client flags?
maria: here's the harness (simplified):
```bash
./replay-harness --trace s3://prod-traces/2026-03-10.json --concurrency 200 --clients 50 --keepalive=0 --reuse_conns=false --protocol=http1
```
kevin: ah — keepalive=0 + reuse_conns=false. that forces a TCP+TLS handshake per request. expensive, especially with small writes and Nagle.
sasha: grpc/http2 multiplexing avoids conn churn. when you force many short-lived http/1 connections you hit SYN/TLS + Nagle tail. did you try --protocol=grpc or keepalive > 30s?
maria: ran keepalive=30s and reuse_conns=true — p95 dropped back. quick numbers: http1 no-reuse p95 210ms; http1 reuse p95 55ms; grpc reuse p95 49ms.
kevin: also check TCP_NODELAY. go net/http may coalesce small writes with Nagle; for token/streaming workloads that matters.
sasha: related note — the kernel-selection patch changed the send path (sendmmsg vs splice) for small scatter-gather writes. in isolation it's fine, but combined with many tiny writes and Nagle it produced head-of-line effects before. could be a batching-heuristic mismatch.
maria: cpu profile shows syscall-heavy behavior on the client/proxy path:
```
perf top sample:
sendmsg 34%
tls_do_handshake 18%
copy_user 12%
context_switches 8%
```
kevin: actionable checklist: 1) make harness default reuse_conns=true 2) add explicit tcp_nodelay flag in harness 3) benchmark grpc channels vs many short http1 connections 4) try proxy keepalive=60s vs default to rule out proxy timeout churn.
sasha: and guarantee apples-to-apples: same inter-arrival distribution + same request size distribution + kv-cache warmup before measuring. synthetic bursts hide long-tail effects.
maria: will run an iso-bench with same inter-arrival distribution, warm up KV cache, and then collect pcap + perf flame.
kevin: for automation add a perf matrix axis: connection-mode={keepalive:on,keepalive:off} x reuse_conns={true,false} x protocol={http1,grpc} x tcp_nodelay={on,off}. run 3 seeds per cell.
maria: :thumbsup: I'll push harness changes + results to perf dashboard and open a PR linking to the kernel-selection change. want reviewers to be aware this is a client/harness artifact, not a runtime perf regression.
sasha: :eyes: if you can attach the client-side pcap it helps — look for clusters of SYN/TLS handshakes aligned with p95 spikes.
infra-bot: deploy-harness job queued (#342) — running with reuse_conns=true, tcp_nodelay=true, protocol=grpc
maria: thanks — will follow up with uploads (pcap + flame) and a short writeup of what to watch for in future benching.
